meta: Giuseppe Valadier's 1810 pen and ink design for an over mantel with a Pompeian-style pavilion and a plan of its dome.
about: Giuseppe Valadier drew this plan of an over mantel in pen and ink in 1810. At top center is part of the framing of the fireplace and the over mantel, a pavilion in Pompeian style with thin columns, shown in perspective. Garland swags hang from its dome, and a small figure stands on top. At the bottom is a plan of the dome in bird's eye view. The Cooper Hewitt describes the sheet in these terms.

meta: Harmen Steenwijck's 1652 still life of four fish on a colander with peaches, berries and a cucumber, made as one of a pair.
about: Four fish lie on a colander beside a branch of peaches, a bucket, a few berries and a cucumber. Harmen Steenwijck painted this still life in 1652 and signed it at lower left as H. Steenwyck. The Rijksmuseum describes it as the pendant of another painting in its collection, which means the two were made to hang as a pair.

meta: Kasparus Karsen's 1846 imaginary view of a riverside town with the cathedral of Aachen, barges at the quay and a ruined tower.
about: An imaginary town on a river has the cathedral of Aachen rising over its roofs. Several barges lie at the quay, a stone bridge stands in the distance, and a dilapidated tower rises at the left. Brick houses line the quay, and small figures walk and talk along it. Kasparus Karsen signed and dated the picture K. Karsen 1846 at lower left. The Rijksmuseum calls the view fantasized.

meta: Pauwels van Hillegaert's 1631 view of Prince Frederik Hendrik at the siege of 's-Hertogenbosch, with a lively army camp.
about: Prince Frederik Hendrik sits on horseback among officers at the left foreground, watching the siege of 's-Hertogenbosch in 1629. In the middle ground is a view into the prince's army camp, where soldiers dance, drink, gamble and fight. In the distance the fortifications and walls of the town can be seen. Pauwels van Hillegaert painted it in 1631. The Rijksmuseum bought it in 1885 from the dealer J. Hollender in Brussels for 800 guilders. It is now on loan to the Nederlands Legermuseum in Delft.

meta: Unkoku Tōgan's pair of folding screens showing the exiled poets Su Shi and Pan Lang, painted in the early 1600s.
about: Pan Lang rides backward on his donkey as he returns from exile, so that he can take a last look at Mount Hua, which he has come to love. Su Shi, in the right screen, sets out on his own journey into exile. Both men were banished by their rulers: Su Shi's comments on economic reforms were read as criticism of the emperor, and Pan Lang composed an ill-advised verse about one of the king's horses. Unkoku Tōgan painted the pair in the early 1600s. He founded the Unkoku school, which emulated the ink painter Sesshū Tōyō, and was official painter to the Mori family.

meta: Wang Meng's Quiet Life in a Wooded Glen, a Yuan dynasty hanging scroll dated 1361 showing a scholar's cottage in the mountains.
about: A modest cottage stands at the foot of towering mountains, and its occupant kneels on a platform playing the zither called qin. A book lies open before him, and young servants wait nearby. The Art Institute of Chicago reads the scene as an image of scholarly retreat from the dusty world of material concerns and political instability. It ties the dry, charcoal-like boulders and the complex, kinetic composition to Wang Meng, the last of the Four Great Masters of the Yuan dynasty. The scroll is dated 1361.

meta: Giovanni da Milano's tempera panel of Christ on the cross with Saint Francis, once looted for Hitler's planned museum in Linz.
about: Christ hangs on the cross while angels catch his blood in chalices. Mary Magdalene and Mary stand at the left, and Saint Francis of Assisi kneels and embraces the cross. At the right stand John and Ignatius of Antioch, and a banderol carries the words Amor meus crucifisus est, which means my love is crucified. Before 1906 the panel belonged to the Amsterdam collector Otto Lanz, who had it as a work by Agnolo Gaddi. His widow sold it with other paintings in 1941 to Hans Posse for Hitler's planned museum in Linz. It was recovered after the war, in 1946.

meta: Francisco Pacheco's Saint John the Baptist, part of an altarpiece for the convent of Santo Ángel in Seville that entered the Prado in 1829.
about: Saint John the Baptist stands full length in a brown garment and a draped red cloak, holding a tall staff topped with a cross and pointing with one hand. A pale halo surrounds his head. Francisco Pacheco painted him for the altarpiece of doña Francisca de León in the church of the convent of Santo Ángel in Seville. He had contracted for the altarpiece in 1605, together with three other paintings. They entered the Prado in 1829, ceded by Dean López Cepero, who had bought them in 1804.

meta: Gustav Richter's 1877 full-length portrait of Emperor Wilhelm I, which passed from Breslau to East Berlin as a gift in 1953.
about: An elderly man with a white mustache and beard stands on a red carpet beside a stone staircase, in a white military tunic with gold braid, a fur-trimmed cape, a sash and decorations. Gustav Richter painted the portrait of Emperor Wilhelm I in 1877. It first belonged to the Association of Christian Merchants in Breslau and hung on loan in the Silesian Museum of Fine Arts there. In 1953 the People's Republic of Poland gave it as a friendship present to the government of the German Democratic Republic, and it passed to the Ministry of Culture in Berlin.

meta: Kano Mitsunobu's folding screens of the Tang emperor Ming Huang and Yang Guifei, based on Bo Juyi's poem Song of Everlasting Sorrow.
about: Bo Juyi's poem Song of Everlasting Sorrow supplies the story for these screens. It tells of the Tang dynasty emperor Ming Huang, also called Xuanzong, and his love for his concubine Yang Guifei, and it was known in Japan since the tenth century. The story unfolds in episodes beginning at the lower right of the left screen and moving counterclockwise. At the top of the left screen a party is held as the An Lushan rebellion begins, and Yang Guifei dies in the uprising. In the upper right of the right screen the emperor is alone after the rebellion ends.

meta: Louis-Philippe Crépin's 1819 painting of the French frigate Poursuivante firing on HMS Hercule in 1803, in a detail of a larger canvas.
about: The French frigate Poursuivante rakes the British ship HMS Hercule with cannon fire in a bay, smoke drifting across the water, in the action of 28 June 1803. Smaller vessels and mounted figures gather on the rocky shore in the foreground. Louis-Philippe Crépin painted the scene in 1819. The Commons record notes that this is a detail of a larger canvas titled Combat de la Poursuivante contre l'Hercule. It belongs to the Musée national de la Marine in Paris.

meta: Chokha's portrait of Maharana Bhim Singh of Mewar with a consort on a swing, painted around 1810 in gum tempera, silver and gold.
about: The Maharana Bhim Singh of Mewar sits with a consort on a pink canopied swing among cushions, his glory marked by a halo behind his head. She folds her hands in devotion. He fondly holds her chin and seems to be putting a garland around her neck, while pink flower petals cover the chamber and yellow garlands hang from it. The Cleveland Museum of Art calls Chokha one of the most celebrated artists in the history of painting at Mewar. It points out a European-style armchair in the background as a sign of British influence at the court. Chokha painted the scene around 1810.
